Subject: TTFT & streaming SLOs - follow-up and qualification

Hi Jamie

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and a couple of qualification questions so our SRE/SE team can size the right config and propose the test plan:

Summary from our side:
- Primary goal: real-time streaming chat for customer-facing product demos (low-latency token-by-token streaming).
- Model: plan to use a 13B open model variant for the pilot.
- Expected usage pattern: interactive sessions ~30-90s, median prompt ~120 tokens, median response ~60-120 tokens.

A few items we need to confirm (answers below will shape capacity + streaming approach):
1) Time-to-first-token (TTFT) target (P95): do you have a hard requirement?
2) Concurrent users / sustained throughput: peak concurrent requests during demo windows and expected sustained RPS outside demos.
3) Streaming preference: SSE vs WebSocket? Any client-side constraints on chunk cadence (max delay between chunks tolerated)?
4) Acceptable chunk sizes (tokens per chunk) or cadence requirements (e.g., typing-like experience vs batch-by-chunk).

Next steps:
- If you can reply with the items above, we'll schedule a 1-hr technical deep-dive with Dylan (SE) and our SREs to finalize the load test window.
- I attached a draft xlsx for streaming requirements to capture cadence and payload examples (streaming_requirements.xlsx).

Thanks
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming SLOs - follow-up and qualification

Thanks Marissa - great summary. A few answers and constraints from our side:

1) TTFT target: Our product team wants TTFT <= 200ms at P95 for short prompts (<128 tokens). For full conversations we can accept up to 300ms P95 but prefer <=250ms if possible.
2) Concurrency/throughput: For the pilot/demo we expect up to 150 concurrent interactive users during scheduled demos. For production: 800 concurrent active users across regions (we expect to stagger). Typical sustained RPS outside demos ~150 RPS.
3) Streaming: We prefer WebSocket streaming (bi-directional) since we do some client-side latency compensation and event ACKing. SSE is acceptable as a fallback for web clients.
4) Chunk cadence: UX team wants token emission to feel like typing - aim for chunk cadence <= 120ms between chunks under normal conditions, and max tolerated gap 250ms. We prefer small chunks (1-4 tokens) when possible.

Also attaching a short doc with sample payloads (pasted below) - happy to walk through in the deep-dive.

Would be good to line up Dylan and an SRE next week.

Jamie
Jamie Lopez

Hi Jamie / Marissa -

Thanks for the clear targets - we can meet these, but there are trade-offs and test steps to validate in your environment. High-level feasibility notes and recommended config before the deep-dive:

Feasibility and recommendation:
- TTFT: Target <=200ms P95 is achievable on Redwood Dedicated capacity with an optimized model path and warm KV cache. On hosted (multi-tenant) we'll typically see ~200-300ms P95 depending on warm state and model variant. For strict <=200ms P95 we recommend Dedicated.
- Streaming transport: WebSocket streaming is recommended for Acme given the need for ACKs and two-way signals; SSE is supported as fallback.
- Chunk cadence & size: To achieve "typing" feel, we recommend emitting small chunks (1-3 tokens) with a typical cadence of 60-120ms between chunks under normal load. We can tune cadence by batching algorithm (time-based vs token-based). Maximum tolerated inter-chunk gap for UX should be <=250ms.
- Throughput/concurrency: For the 150-concurrent pilot we can run on a single 4-GPU Dedicated pool (model/quantization-dependent). For production ~800 concurrent active users, we'd propose autoscaling across multiple pools with a target of ~200-300 effective concurrent streams per pool.

Planned validation/test steps:
1) Smoke test on hosted to measure baseline TTFT with the provided sample payloads (Marissa will schedule).
2) Dedicated capacity benchmark: warm model, run 10-min sustained load at pilot concurrency (150 concurrent) and measure P50/P95/P99 for TTFT and chunk cadence.
3) Simulated client tests (browser + mobile): validate WebSocket handshake, keep-alive and chunk reassembly behavior. We'll test worst-case network conditions (50-150ms RTT) to measure inter-chunk gaps.

Data we need from Acme before tests:
- Representative payloads and maximum request size (you attached an xlsx, but please confirm final examples).
- Client list (desktop web/mobile/webview) and any proxies/edge gateways that may affect WebSocket.
- Preferred test window and a test account with sample data.

- Thu, 9 Apr 2026 14:00-15:00 PT

Happy to talk through any detail in the deep-dive.
